newsitem.title: COMOROS: Indian Ocean islands plan to attract more tourists.
newsitem.headline: Indian Ocean islands plan to attract more tourists.

text.p: The Comoros, Madagascar, Mauritius, Reunion and the Seychelles agreed on plans to boost tourism in the Indian Ocean islands with aid from the European Union, delegates said on Sunday.

After the two-day conference in the Comoro Islands capital Moroni, the leader of the Seychelles delegation Maurice Lalanne said: "We intend to transform the Indian Ocean islands into a major target area for tomorrow's tourists."
He said the five states would co-operate in marketing their tourism attractions in an $8.8 million programme offering everything from beach holidays to adventure tourism.
The target is 1.5 million tourists a year by the end of the century, against the 950,000 achieved last year -- with cruise ships accounting for a quarter of the total.

Conference sources said the Reunion airline, Air Australe, was launching a new "Indian Ocean Pass" to encourage tourists to visit more than one of the island destinations, with attractive reductions against normal air fares. Reunion is French overseas territory.
They said the tourism pattern in the area varied considerably, with Mauritius attracting 422,000 tourists last year against only 25,000 for the Comoros.
